      title: Owner fields

        firstName:
          title: First name

          type: string
          minLength: 1

          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80

          title: Telephone number

## Summary

Added optional owner `email` — stored and returned lower-cased, rejected with 400 when present but syntactically invalid. I kept structural impact low by adding a small, cohesive step + escalation rather than growing any existing class, and never modified an existing function body.

**New small units (each ~one trivial method, no surrounding complexity):**
- `NormalizeOwnerEmail.java` — POST-pipeline step: skips a missing email, lower-cases a valid one in place, throws on an invalid one.
- `InvalidOwnerEmailException.java` + `InvalidOwnerEmailExceptionHandler.java` — dedicated checked exception → 400, matching the codebase's existing per-concern escalation pattern (e.g. `DuplicateTelephoneException`).
- Escalation YAML wiring the exception to its handler.

- `Owner.java` — added the `email` field + plain accessors (new methods only; no existing method touched).

- `owners.POST.yml` — inserted the `normalizeEmail` step into the pipeline.
- `db/hsqldb/schema.sql` — added the `email` column; `data.sql` — extended the positional seed inserts to match.

**Scope note:** the spec and tests cover create + read-back. The PUT/update path was intentionally left untouched to avoid growing `ApplyOwner`; email is not currently editable via PUT. Let me know if you'd like update support too.
